coverage: Both full English editions, all twelve books: named people, gods, personified powers, named monsters and named peoples. Places, rivers as geography, mountains, islands and ships are excluded — the boat race in book five names four galleys after monsters, and those occurrences are not cast.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: Son of Venus and Anchises, leader of the Trojan survivors and the man the poem follows from burning Troy to Italy.

entities.name: Turnus
entities.body: King of the Rutulians, betrothed to Lavinia before the Trojans came, and Aeneas’s enemy through the second half of the poem.

entities.name: Dido
entities.body: Queen and founder of Carthage, a widow who fled Tyre after her brother murdered her husband. The poem also calls her Eliza.

entities.name: Ascanius
entities.body: Aeneas’s young son, also called Iulus, from whom Rome’s Julian line is traced.

entities.name: Anchises
entities.body: Aeneas’s father, carried out of Troy on his son’s shoulders.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: Goddess of love and Aeneas’s mother, who works constantly on his behalf.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: Queen of the gods, who hates the Trojans and drives the whole action against them. The poem also calls her Saturnia.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: King of the gods, who holds to the fate promised the Trojans. The poem also calls him Jupiter and the Thunderer.

entities.name: Latinus
entities.body: King of Latium, Lavinia’s father, who would give his daughter to Aeneas.

entities.name: Lavinia
entities.body: Latinus’s only daughter and heiress, promised first to Turnus and then to Aeneas.

entities.name: Amata
entities.body: Latinus’s queen, who wants Turnus for a son-in-law and is driven mad by the Fury.

entities.name: Evander
entities.body: The old Arcadian king at Pallanteum on the future site of Rome, who allies with Aeneas.

entities.name: Pallas
entities.body: Evander’s young son, sent to war under Aeneas’s protection.

entities.name: Pallas
entities.body: Minerva under her Greek by-name; the goddess who helped ruin Troy and whose temple and image recur through the poem.

entities.name: Pallas
entities.body: Evander’s great-grandsire, after whom the town of Pallanteum is named.

entities.name: Mezentius
entities.body: The exiled Etruscan tyrant, a contemner of the gods, who fights for Turnus.

entities.name: Lausus
entities.body: Mezentius’s son, the handsomest of the Italian youth, who dies defending his father.

entities.name: Camilla
entities.body: The Volscian warrior queen, raised to the hunt and the spear, who leads her troops for Turnus.

entities.name: Achates
entities.body: Aeneas’s closest companion, called faithful throughout.

entities.name: The Sibyl
entities.body: The prophetess of Cumae, Apollo’s and Diana’s priestess, who guides Aeneas through the underworld. Her name is Deiphobe.

entities.name: Priam
entities.body: The old king of Troy, killed at his own altar on the night the city fell.

entities.name: Hector
entities.body: Priam’s son and Troy’s great defender, already dead when the poem opens; his ghost warns Aeneas to flee.

entities.name: Creusa
entities.body: Aeneas’s first wife, lost in the sack of Troy; her ghost sends him on to Italy.

entities.name: Anna
entities.body: Dido’s sister and confidante.

entities.name: Nisus
entities.body: A Trojan, son of Hyrtacus, famous for his devotion to Euryalus; the two go out together on the night raid.

entities.name: Euryalus
entities.body: A Trojan boy of great beauty, Nisus’s inseparable friend.

entities.name: Acestes
entities.body: King of the Sicilian Trojans, born of Trojan parentage, who twice receives Aeneas’s fleet.

entities.name: Mnestheus
entities.body: A Trojan captain, founder of the Memmian line, who commands in Aeneas’s absence.

entities.name: Serestus
entities.body: A Trojan captain who walks the camp with Mnestheus. Dryden spells him Serestus once and Seresthus elsewhere.

entities.name: Cloanthus
entities.body: A Trojan captain, founder of the Cluentian line, who wins the boat race.

entities.name: Ilioneus
entities.body: The eldest and gravest of the Trojan captains, who speaks for them to Dido and to Latinus.

entities.name: Sergesthus
entities.body: A Trojan captain, founder of the Sergian line, whose galley is wrecked on the rocks in the boat race.

entities.name: Messapus
entities.body: A Latin captain, Neptune’s son, whom no steel can wound.

entities.name: Drances
entities.body: A Latin elder, a powerful speaker and Turnus’s bitter opponent in council.

entities.name: Juturna
entities.body: Turnus’s sister, a nymph made immortal by Jove, who keeps her brother from his death as long as she can.

entities.name: Tarchon
entities.body: The Etruscan chief who brings his people to Aeneas.

entities.name: Helenus
entities.body: Priam’s son, a seer, now reigning in Epirus with Andromache; he tells Aeneas his route.

entities.name: Andromache
entities.body: Hector’s widow, taken by Pyrrhus and afterwards married to Helenus.

entities.name: Palinurus
entities.body: Aeneas’s helmsman, lost overboard off the Italian coast.

entities.name: Misenus
entities.body: Aeneas’s trumpeter, once Hector’s, who challenges the sea gods and drowns for it.

entities.name: Sinon
entities.body: The Greek who lets himself be captured and talks Troy into taking in the horse.

entities.name: Laocoon
entities.body: Neptune’s priest at Troy, who warns against the horse and is killed with his sons by serpents. The modern edition spells him Laocoön.

entities.name: Pyrrhus
entities.body: Achilles’ son, who kills Priam at the altar; also called Neoptolemus.

entities.name: Ulysses
entities.body: The Greek whose cunning the Trojans blame for their ruin; the poem also calls him Ithacus.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: The greatest of the Greeks at Troy, dead before the poem begins; also called Pelides.

entities.name: Diomede
entities.body: A Greek captain at Troy, now settled in Italy, who refuses to join the war against Aeneas. The poem spells him Diomede and Diomedes.

entities.name: Aeolus
entities.body: King of the winds, who looses the storm at Juno’s request.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: God of the sea, who calms the storm and later demands one life for the fleet’s safe passage.

entities.name: Mercury
entities.body: The messenger god, sent to move Aeneas out of Carthage. The poem also calls him Cyllenius and, in the modern edition, Hermes.

entities.name: Iris
entities.body: Juno’s messenger, who comes down on the rainbow.

entities.name: Alecto
entities.body: The Fury Juno raises out of hell to break the peace.

entities.name: Vulcan
entities.body: The smith of the gods, who forges Aeneas’s shield at Venus’s asking. Called the Lemnian god and Mulciber.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: God of prophecy and archery, whose oracles direct the Trojans; called Phoebus and the Delian god.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: Goddess of the hunt and the moon; called Phoebe, Trivia and Cynthia.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: God of war.

entities.name: Minerva
entities.body: Goddess of war and craft; the poem more often calls her Pallas.

entities.name: Saturn
entities.body: The old god who ruled Latium in the golden age, Jove’s father.

entities.name: Pluto
entities.body: King of the dead, whose palace Aeneas must visit.

entities.name: Proserpine
entities.body: Queen of the dead, whose golden bough Aeneas must carry.

entities.name: Hecate
entities.body: The threefold goddess of the crossroads, invoked in Dido’s rites.

entities.name: Ceres
entities.body: Goddess of the harvest, whose ruined temple is the Trojans’ meeting point.

entities.name: Bacchus
entities.body: God of wine, invoked at the Carthaginian feast.

entities.name: Cybele
entities.body: The mother of the gods, whose pines become Aeneas’s ships.

entities.name: Vesta
entities.body: Goddess of the hearth, whose relics Aeneas carries out of Troy.

entities.name: Latona
entities.body: Mother of Apollo and Diana.

entities.name: Aurora
entities.body: The dawn goddess, who leaves her saffron bed each morning.

entities.name: Boreas
entities.body: The north wind.

entities.name: Eurus
entities.body: The east wind, who drives three ships onto the shoals.

entities.name: Triton
entities.body: A sea god who heaves the stranded ships off the rocks.

entities.name: The Nereids
entities.body: The sea nymphs; Aeneas’s ships are turned into them.

entities.name: Cymothoe
entities.body: A sea nymph who helps free the grounded ships.

entities.name: Doto
entities.body: A sea nymph, named when the ships are promised her shape.

entities.name: The Harpies
entities.body: The foul bird-women of the Strophades, who befoul the Trojans’ meal.

entities.name: Celaeno
entities.body: The Harpies’ leader, who prophesies that hunger will make the Trojans eat their tables.

entities.name: Charon
entities.body: The ferryman of the dead.

entities.name: Cerberus
entities.body: The three-headed dog at the gate of the underworld.

entities.name: The Furies
entities.body: The avenging sisters of hell; the poem also names them the Dirae.

entities.name: Fame
entities.body: Rumour personified, the swiftest of evils, who grows as she goes and spreads the news of Dido and Aeneas.

entities.name: Hymen
entities.body: The god of marriage, invoked for the union in the cave.

entities.name: Faunus
entities.body: A god of the Latin woods, Latinus’s father.

entities.name: Picus
entities.body: Faunus’s father, a king turned into a bird, whose image stands in Latinus’s hall.

entities.name: Marica
entities.body: A Laurentian nymph, Latinus’s mother.

entities.name: Janus
entities.body: The two-faced god whose gates stand open in war.

entities.name: Quirinus
entities.body: Romulus under his divine name.

entities.name: Bellona
entities.body: The war goddess, who leads the bride to her wedding.

entities.name: Feronia
entities.body: A goddess whose grove and temple stand by Lake Ciminius.

entities.name: Carmenta
entities.body: Evander’s mother, a prophetess who foretold the Roman race.

entities.name: The river god Tiber
entities.body: The river of Latium, who rises in a dream to tell Aeneas he has reached his promised land.

entities.name: Atlas
entities.body: The Titan whose head sustains the sky; Mercury’s grandfather and Dardanus’s ancestor.

entities.name: Maia
entities.body: Mercury’s mother, Atlas’s daughter.

entities.name: Chaos
entities.body: A power of the world below, invoked in Dido’s rites.

entities.name: Erebus
entities.body: The darkness of the world below, invoked as a power.

entities.name: Sleep
entities.body: The god who slides down to Palinurus at the helm.

entities.name: The Muses
entities.body: The goddesses of song, called on to open the catalogue of Italian chiefs.

entities.name: Erato
entities.body: The Muse invoked at the poem’s second opening.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The sisters who spin and cut the thread of every life.

entities.name: Abas
entities.body: A Trojan captain whose ship is disabled in the opening storm.

entities.name: Abas
entities.body: A Greek whose brazen shield Aeneas hung on the temple door at Actium.

entities.name: Abas
entities.body: An Etruscan captain in Aeneas’s alliance, killed by Mezentius.

entities.name: Orontes
entities.body: Captain of the Lycian ship, lost with all hands in the storm.

entities.name: Gyas
entities.body: A Trojan captain, who commands the Chimaera in the boat race and loses it by temper.

entities.name: Gyas
entities.body: An Italian of monstrous bulk, killed by Aeneas.

entities.name: Lycus
entities.body: A Trojan captain given up for lost after the storm.

entities.name: Lycus
entities.body: A young Trojan who escapes the burning tower and is run down by Turnus.

entities.name: Amycus
entities.body: A Trojan captain given up for lost after the storm.

entities.name: Amycus
entities.body: A Trojan huntsman, skilled in poisoned darts, killed by Turnus in the camp.

entities.name: Amycus
entities.body: An Italian whom Turnus throws from his horse, one of two brothers killed together.

entities.name: Alethes
entities.body: The oldest of the Trojan counsellors, who blesses Nisus and Euryalus.

entities.name: Capys
entities.body: A Trojan captain.

entities.name: Capys
entities.body: An Alban king in the parade of Aeneas’s descendants.

entities.name: Antheus
entities.body: A Trojan captain.

entities.name: Caicus
entities.body: A Trojan captain.

entities.name: Bitias
entities.body: A Tyrian lord at Dido’s feast, the first to take up the challenge of the cup.

entities.name: Bitias
entities.body: A giant Trojan, son of Alcanor and the nymph Hiera, who opens the camp gate and dies for it.

entities.name: Pandarus
entities.body: A giant Trojan, Bitias’s brother, who shuts Turnus inside the camp and is killed by him.

entities.name: Pandarus
entities.body: The Lycian archer who broke the truce at Troy, named as Eurytion’s brother.

entities.name: Alcanor
entities.body: Father of the giant brothers Pandarus and Bitias.

entities.name: Alcanor
entities.body: An Italian who reaches out to save his wounded brother and is maimed by Aeneas.

entities.name: Hiera
entities.body: The nymph who bore Pandarus and Bitias on Ida.

entities.name: Helymus
entities.body: A Sicilian of Acestes’ following who runs in the foot race.

entities.name: Panopes
entities.body: A Sicilian huntsman of Acestes’ following.

entities.name: Salius
entities.body: An Acarnanian in Acestes’ following who is tripped in the foot race and claims the prize.

entities.name: Patron
entities.body: An Arcadian in Acestes’ following who runs in the foot race.

entities.name: Diores
entities.body: A Trojan of Priam’s royal line, third in the foot race.

entities.name: Entellus
entities.body: The old Sicilian boxer, Eryx’s pupil, who takes up Dares’ challenge.

entities.name: Dares
entities.body: The Trojan boxer who challenges all comers and is beaten by Entellus.

entities.name: Eryx
entities.body: The old boxer and king of Sicily, Entellus’s master, whose gauntlets are produced.

entities.name: Hippocoon
entities.body: A Trojan whose lot is drawn first in the archery contest.

entities.name: Eurytion
entities.body: A Trojan archer, brother of the Lycian Pandarus, who brings down the dove.

entities.name: Atys
entities.body: A Trojan boy brought up with Iulus, who leads the second squadron in the riding display.

entities.name: Nautes
entities.body: The old Trojan seer who advises leaving the weary behind in Sicily.

entities.name: Beroe
entities.body: Doryclus’s aged wife, whose shape Iris takes to fire the Trojan ships.

entities.name: Doryclus
entities.body: Beroe’s husband, of Tmarus.

entities.name: Pyrgo
entities.body: The old nurse of Priam’s children, who sees through Iris’s disguise.

entities.name: Acmon
entities.body: A Trojan of Sarpedon’s blood who holds the wall with his brother.

entities.name: Asius
entities.body: A Trojan of Sarpedon’s blood who holds the wall with his brother.

entities.name: Haemon
entities.body: A young Trojan at the defence of the wall.

entities.name: Caeneus
entities.body: A Trojan who kills Ortygius at the wall and is killed by Turnus.

entities.name: Caeneus
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning, once a woman and once a man.

entities.name: Helenor
entities.body: A Lydian king’s bastard son by the slave Licymnia, who leaps from the burning tower and dies fighting.

entities.name: Licymnia
entities.body: The slave who bore Helenor and sent him secretly to Troy.

entities.name: Idaeus
entities.body: A Trojan sent with Actor to carry Euryalus’s mother away.

entities.name: Idaeus
entities.body: Priam’s charioteer, seen among the shades.

entities.name: Actor
entities.body: A Trojan sent with Idaeus to carry Euryalus’s mother away.

entities.name: Actor
entities.body: An Auruncan whose great lance Turnus took and wields.

entities.name: Corynaeus
entities.body: A Trojan priest, who performs the rites at Misenus’s funeral and later fights with a brand from his own altar.

entities.name: Achaemenides
entities.body: A Greek of Ithaca left behind in the Cyclops’ country, taken aboard by the Trojans.

entities.name: Acoetes
entities.body: Evander’s old squire, sent with Pallas and left to watch his body.

entities.name: Iapyx
entities.body: The physician who tends Aeneas’s wound; Apollo’s favourite, who chose healing over prophecy.

entities.name: Ufens
entities.body: A Latin captain who leads the mountain troops of Nursia.

entities.name: Halesus
entities.body: A captain born of Agamemnon’s line, a lifelong enemy of Troy, who brings his people to Turnus.

entities.name: Aventinus
entities.body: Hercules’ son by the priestess Rhea, who comes to the war with his father’s lion skin.

entities.name: Rhea
entities.body: The priestess whom Hercules found on the Aventine; Aventinus’s mother.

entities.name: Catillus
entities.body: One of the three brothers of Tibur, who lead Argive horse for Turnus.

entities.name: Coras
entities.body: One of the three brothers of Tibur, who lead Argive horse for Turnus.

entities.name: Tiburs
entities.body: The brother who gave Tibur its name.

entities.name: Caeculus
entities.body: The founder of Praeneste, said to be Vulcan’s son, found in the fire.

entities.name: Clausus
entities.body: A Sabine captain who is an army in himself, and the founder of the Claudian house.

entities.name: Virbius
entities.body: Hippolytus’s son, named for his father’s second life, who comes to the war from Aricia’s groves.

entities.name: Hippolytus
entities.body: Theseus’s son, torn apart by his horses and restored to life by the healing god.

entities.name: Aricia
entities.body: Hippolytus’s wife, who bore Virbius in the Egerian groves.

entities.name: Tyrrheus
entities.body: Latinus’s chief ranger, whose tame stag the Trojans shoot.

entities.name: Silvia
entities.body: Tyrrheus’s daughter, who reared the stag.

entities.name: Almon
entities.body: Tyrrheus’s eldest son, the first man killed in the new war.

entities.name: Venulus
entities.body: The Latin envoy sent to ask Diomede for help.

entities.name: Tolumnius
entities.body: The Latins’ augur, who reads the omen and throws the spear that breaks the truce.

entities.name: Camers
entities.body: A rich young Latin, Volscens’s son, killed by Aeneas.

entities.name: Numa
entities.body: A strong young Latin killed by Aeneas.

entities.name: Volscens
entities.body: The Latin cavalry commander who kills Euryalus and is killed by Nisus.

entities.name: Rhamnes
entities.body: An augur and Turnus’s favourite, killed asleep by Nisus.

entities.name: Remus
entities.body: A Rutulian killed in his sleep with his armour-bearer and his slaves.

entities.name: Remus
entities.body: Romulus’s brother, named in the promise of a Rome at peace.

entities.name: Romulus
entities.body: The wolf-suckled founder of Rome, Mars’s son by Ilia.

entities.name: Ilia
entities.body: The priestess who bears Romulus and Remus to Mars.

entities.name: Serranus
entities.body: A fair young Rutulian killed in his sleep.

entities.name: Lamus
entities.body: A Rutulian killed in his sleep by Nisus.

entities.name: Lamyrus
entities.body: A Rutulian killed in his sleep by Nisus.

entities.name: Rhoetus
entities.body: A Rutulian who wakes and hides behind a jar, and is killed by Euryalus.

entities.name: Fadus
entities.body: A Rutulian killed by Euryalus.

entities.name: Hebesus
entities.body: A Rutulian killed by Euryalus.

entities.name: Caedicus
entities.body: A rich man who gave Remulus the golden belt that Euryalus takes.

entities.name: Remulus
entities.body: A Tiburtine to whom Caedicus gave the belt; his heir wore it until the Ardeans took it.

entities.name: Sulmo
entities.body: A Rutulian speared in the back during the night pursuit.

entities.name: Tagus
entities.body: A Rutulian killed beside Sulmo.

entities.name: Numanus
entities.body: Turnus’s brother-in-law, who taunts the Trojans and is shot by Ascanius.

entities.name: Lucetius
entities.body: A Rutulian crushed by a rock as he brings fire to the gate.

entities.name: Ortygius
entities.body: A Rutulian killed by Caeneus.

entities.name: Itys
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus at the wall.

entities.name: Clonius
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus at the wall.

entities.name: Sagar
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus at the wall.

entities.name: Ida
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus while standing on the wall.

entities.name: Privernus
entities.body: A Trojan killed at the wall after clapping his hand to a slight wound.

entities.name: Themilla
entities.body: A Rutulian who gives Privernus his first, slight wound.

entities.name: Antiphates
entities.body: Sarpedon’s bastard son by a Theban slave, the first man Turnus meets inside the camp.

entities.name: Meropes
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus inside the camp.

entities.name: Erymanthus
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus inside the camp.

entities.name: Aphidnus
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus inside the camp.

entities.name: Quercens
entities.body: A Rutulian who rushes the open gate.

entities.name: Tmarus
entities.body: A Rutulian who rushes the open gate.

entities.name: Equicolus
entities.body: A Rutulian in bright armour who rushes the open gate.

entities.name: Clytius
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Turnus inside the camp.

entities.name: Lucagus
entities.body: A Latin who fights from the chariot his brother Liger drives; killed by Aeneas.

entities.name: Liger
entities.body: Lucagus’s brother, who drives their chariot and taunts Aeneas.

entities.name: Asylas
entities.body: An Etruscan captain and diviner, who reads the stars and the flight of birds, and leads the chase.

entities.name: Mimas
entities.body: A Trojan born the same night as Paris, killed by Mezentius.

entities.name: Evas
entities.body: A Trojan killed by Mezentius.

entities.name: Orsilochus
entities.body: A Trojan who does not dare face Camilla and is killed by her.

entities.name: Butes
entities.body: The giant of Amycus’s Bebrycian stock whom Eryx beat at Hector’s funeral games.

entities.name: Butes
entities.body: Anchises’ old squire, left to attend Ascanius; Apollo takes his shape.

entities.name: Butes
entities.body: A bulky Trojan killed breast to breast by Camilla.

entities.name: Butes
entities.body: A Trojan thrown by his floundering horse and killed by Turnus.

entities.name: Thoas
entities.body: One of the Greeks who came down out of the wooden horse.

entities.name: Thoas
entities.body: A warrior struck in the forehead with a stone by Pallas.

entities.name: Menoetes
entities.body: Gyas’s pilot in the boat race, thrown overboard for steering too cautiously.

entities.name: Menoetes
entities.body: A peaceful Arcadian who had long shunned war, killed by Turnus.

entities.name: Rhoeteus
entities.body: A man who crosses the plain by chance and takes the spear Pallas meant for Ilus.

entities.name: Ilus
entities.body: Tros’s son, an ancestor of the Trojan house, enjoying fame in Elysium.

entities.name: Ilus
entities.body: The man Pallas aimed at when Rhoeteus crossed the flight of the spear.

entities.name: Herminius
entities.body: The mighty champion of the Tuscan crew, killed by Catillus.

entities.name: Iolas
entities.body: A man killed by Catillus.

entities.name: Aruns
entities.body: The Etruscan who stalks Camilla, kills her from cover and is killed by Diana’s nymph.

entities.name: Opis
entities.body: Diana’s nymph, sent to avenge Camilla.

entities.name: Metiscus
entities.body: Turnus’s charioteer, whose shape Juturna takes.

entities.name: Acca
entities.body: Camilla’s companion, sent to carry her last message to Turnus.

entities.name: Cydon
entities.body: A Latin whom Aeneas spares the doom of, and whose seven brothers attack.

entities.name: Dryops
entities.body: A Trojan speared through the throat by Clausus.

entities.name: Hyarbas
entities.body: The African king who courted Dido and prays to Jove against her Trojan guest. The modern edition spells him Iarbas.

entities.name: Sychaeus
entities.body: Dido’s murdered husband, whose ghost tells her to flee Tyre.

entities.name: Pygmalion
entities.body: Dido’s brother, king of Tyre, who murdered Sychaeus for his wealth.

entities.name: Belus
entities.body: Dido’s father, who once conquered Cyprus.

entities.name: Barce
entities.body: Sychaeus’s old nurse, whom Dido sends away at the end.

entities.name: Daunus
entities.body: Turnus’s father.

entities.name: Pilumnus
entities.body: Turnus’s ancestor, a god four generations back.

entities.name: Dardanus
entities.body: Founder of the Trojan line, born in Italy, which makes Italy the Trojans’ ancient mother.

entities.name: Iasius
entities.body: Dardanus’s brother, born in the same country.

entities.name: Teucer
entities.body: The ancestor from Crete whose name the Trojans bear.

entities.name: Teucer
entities.body: The exile from Salamis who once came to Sidon and was helped by Belus.

entities.name: Assaracus
entities.body: An ancestor of the Trojan house, enjoying fame in Elysium.

entities.name: Laomedon
entities.body: Priam’s father, whose broken faith is held against Troy.

entities.name: Ganymede
entities.body: The Trojan boy carried up to serve Jove, one of Juno’s standing grievances.

entities.name: Electra
entities.body: Atlas’s daughter and Dardanus’s mother, another of Juno’s grievances.

entities.name: Paris
entities.body: The Trojan whose judgment against Juno began her hatred, and who carried Helen away.

entities.name: Helen
entities.body: Menelaus’s wife, carried off by Paris; Aeneas finds her hiding at Vesta’s shrine.

entities.name: Orestes
entities.body: Agamemnon’s son, who kills Pyrrhus at his father’s altar.

entities.name: Agamemnon
entities.body: The Greek commander at Troy.

entities.name: Menelaus
entities.body: Helen’s husband and Agamemnon’s brother.

entities.name: Atreus
entities.body: Father of the two brother kings.

entities.name: Calchas
entities.body: The Greek augur whose word Sinon uses to frame his story.

entities.name: Palamedes
entities.body: The Greek Sinon claims as his kinsman, put to death on a false charge.

entities.name: Thymoetes
entities.body: The Trojan who urges bringing the horse inside.

entities.name: Cassandra
entities.body: Priam’s daughter, whose true prophecies Apollo doomed to be disbelieved.

entities.name: Coroebus
entities.body: Cassandra’s suitor, killed at Pallas’s altar on the night Troy fell.

entities.name: Ripheus
entities.body: The justest of the Trojans, killed on the night Troy fell.

entities.name: Iphitus
entities.body: An aged Trojan who fights at Aeneas’s side on the last night.

entities.name: Dymas
entities.body: A Trojan who joins Aeneas’s band on the last night.

entities.name: Hypanis
entities.body: A Trojan who joins Aeneas’s band on the last night.

entities.name: Pantheus
entities.body: Apollo’s priest on the citadel, who brings Aeneas the household gods.

entities.name: Androgeos
entities.body: The Greek captain who mistakes Aeneas’s band for his own men.

entities.name: Peneleus
entities.body: The Greek who kills Coroebus at Pallas’s altar.

entities.name: Polites
entities.body: Priam’s son, run down and killed in front of his parents.

entities.name: Hecuba
entities.body: Priam’s queen, sheltering at the altar with her daughters.

entities.name: Polydorus
entities.body: Priam’s youngest son, murdered for his gold in Thrace; his voice comes out of the ground. Dryden calls him Polydore.

entities.name: Lycurgus
entities.body: The fierce king who once ruled Thrace.

entities.name: Idomeneus
entities.body: The Cretan king driven out of his own country, which leaves Crete open.

entities.name: Anius
entities.body: The priest-king of Delos, Anchises’ old guest-friend.

entities.name: Deiphobus
entities.body: Priam’s son, whose house burns first, and whose mutilated shade Aeneas meets below.

entities.name: Sthenelus
entities.body: One of the Greeks who comes out of the horse.

entities.name: Tysander
entities.body: One of the Greeks who comes out of the horse.

entities.name: Athamas
entities.body: One of the Greeks who comes out of the horse.

entities.name: Epeus
entities.body: The Greek who built the horse.

entities.name: Demoleus
entities.body: A Greek from whom Aeneas took a coat of mail.

entities.name: Cisseus
entities.body: The Thracian who gave Anchises a figured goblet.

entities.name: Marcellus
entities.body: The young Roman in the parade of souls whose early death the poem mourns.

entities.name: Caesar
entities.body: The ruler promised to rise from the Julian line.

entities.name: Numitor
entities.body: An Alban king in the parade of Aeneas’s descendants.

entities.name: Procas
entities.body: An Alban king in the parade of Aeneas’s descendants.

entities.name: Silvius
entities.body: Aeneas’s last-begotten son, born in the woods to Lavinia.

entities.name: Silvius Aeneas
entities.body: A later Alban king who bears Aeneas’s name.

entities.name: Tullus
entities.body: An early Roman king in the parade of souls.

entities.name: Ancus
entities.body: An early Roman king in the parade of souls.

entities.name: Tarquin
entities.body: The Roman kings whose line the avenging sword ends.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: The Roman who put his own sons to death for the republic.

entities.name: Cato
entities.body: The Roman renowned for gravity, seen in the parade of souls.

entities.name: Cossus
entities.body: A conquering Roman seen in the parade of souls.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The hero who killed Cacus on the future site of Rome, worshipped there ever since. The poem also calls him Alcides.

entities.name: Cacus
entities.body: The fire-breathing monster of the Aventine cave, killed by Hercules.

entities.name: Geryon
entities.body: The triple-bodied giant Hercules killed in Spain.

entities.name: Potitius
entities.body: The founder of Hercules’ annual rites at Rome.

entities.name: Evadne
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning.

entities.name: Laodamia
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning.

entities.name: Pasiphae
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning; the modern edition spells her Pasiphaë.

entities.name: Phaedra
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning.

entities.name: Procris
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning.

entities.name: Eriphyle
entities.body: A shade in the fields of mourning.

entities.name: Theseus
entities.body: The hero seated for ever in the underworld.

entities.name: Pirithous
entities.body: Theseus’s companion, punished below; the modern edition spells him Peirithous.

entities.name: Minos
entities.body: The judge who shakes the urn over the silent shades.

entities.name: Rhadamanthus
entities.body: The judge of the guilty in Tartarus.

entities.name: Tisiphone
entities.body: The Fury who keeps the gate of Tartarus.

entities.name: Salmoneus
entities.body: The shade punished for counterfeiting Jove’s thunder.

entities.name: Tityus
entities.body: The giant whose liver the vulture feeds on for ever.

entities.name: Ixion
entities.body: A shade punished in Tartarus.

entities.name: Phlegyas
entities.body: The shade who cries out a warning to learn justice.

entities.name: Musaeus
entities.body: The divine singer among the blessed, who shows the way to Anchises.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The Thracian singer, seen among the blessed in his long robe.

entities.name: Memnon
entities.body: The swarthy warrior in the Carthaginian frescoes.

entities.name: Penthesilea
entities.body: The Amazon queen in the Carthaginian frescoes. Dryden spells her Penthisilea.

entities.name: Troilus
entities.body: Priam’s young son, dragged behind his chariot in the frescoes.

entities.name: Sarpedon
entities.body: The Lycian who fell at Troy, named as father of the brothers who hold the wall.

entities.name: Glaucus
entities.body: One of Antenor’s sons, seen among the shades of the Trojan dead.

entities.name: Medon
entities.body: One of Antenor’s sons, seen among the shades of the Trojan dead.

entities.name: Antenor
entities.body: The Trojan who escaped and founded Padua, cited as a precedent by Venus.

entities.name: Harpalyce
entities.body: The Thracian huntress Venus is compared to.

entities.name: Iopas
entities.body: The long-haired bard who sings at Dido’s feast.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: Venus’s son, sent to Carthage in Ascanius’s shape to fire Dido with love.

entities.name: The Amazons
entities.body: The warrior women of the frescoes and of Camilla’s comparison.

entities.name: The Cyclops
entities.body: The one-eyed giants of Sicily; Polyphemus is their most famous. Dryden spells the singular Polypheme.

entities.name: Polyphemus
entities.body: The blinded Cyclops whom the Trojans see groping down to the sea. Dryden calls him Polypheme.

entities.name: Scylla
entities.body: The monster whose waist ends in dogs, waiting on the right of the strait.

entities.name: Charybdis
entities.body: The whirlpool on the left of the strait, which swallows and spews the sea three times a day.

entities.name: The Chimaera
entities.body: The fire-breathing monster, seen at the gate of hell and blazoned on Turnus’s crest.

entities.name: The Centaurs
entities.body: The double-shaped creatures who besiege the gate of hell.

entities.name: Briareus
entities.body: The hundred-handed monster at the gate of hell.

entities.name: The Gorgons
entities.body: Monsters at the gate of hell.

entities.name: The Hydra
entities.body: The many-headed monster at the gate of hell, and in Lerna’s lake.

entities.name: Typhoeus
entities.body: A monster named among the terrors Hercules did not fear.

entities.name: The Trojans
entities.body: Aeneas’s people, the survivors of Troy; also called Dardans, Phrygians and Teucrians.

entities.name: The Latins
entities.body: Latinus’s people, whose land the Trojans are fated to hold.

entities.name: The Rutulians
entities.body: Turnus’s people, of Ardea.

entities.name: The Tyrians
entities.body: Dido’s people, the settlers of Carthage.

entities.name: The Greeks
entities.body: The army that took Troy; the poem also calls them Grecians, Argives and Danaans.

entities.name: The Arcadians
entities.body: Evander’s people at Pallanteum.

entities.name: The Tuscans
entities.body: The Etruscan people who rise against Mezentius and join Aeneas.

entities.name: The Volscians
entities.body: Camilla’s people.

entities.name: The Italians
entities.body: The peoples of Italy taken together; also called Ausonians and Oenotrians.

entities.name: The Auruncans
entities.body: An Italian people from the hills who join Turnus.

entities.name: The Equicolae
entities.body: A rough Italian people under Ufens; the modern edition spells them Equicoli.

entities.name: The Faliscans
entities.body: An Italian people called to the war.

entities.name: The Sicanians
entities.body: An old people of Sicily and Italy.

entities.name: The Numidians
entities.body: An African people on Carthage’s frontier.

entities.name: The Gauls
entities.body: The people whose night attack on the Capitol the geese betrayed, shown on Aeneas’s shield.

entities.name: The Scythians
entities.body: A far northern people, named among those Rome will face.
